How do you handle flaky integration tests?

ana_dev · 12 March · 14 replies

We have about forty integration tests that hit a real Postgres instance, and roughly three of them fail once every twenty runs for reasons nobody can reproduce locally.

Retrying the whole suite hides the problem, but quarantining the tests means they never get fixed. What actually works for teams here?

Report · Quote
ben_ops · 12 March

The first thing I would do is make each test own its database schema and run in its own transaction, so tests cannot see each other's rows. Most flakiness I have seen came from shared state, not from the database itself.

After that, log the queries and timings for failures only. Once you have a month of those logs the pattern is usually obvious.

— Ben, platform team at a payments startup
cleo_writes · 13 March

Quarantine is fine if it comes with a deadline and an owner. We mark a flaky test with a ticket number and an expiry date, and the build fails when the date passes. It is annoying, which is the point.

— Cleo, quality engineering
dmitri · 13 March

Also check the clock. We had a test that failed only when the suite crossed midnight in the CI runner's timezone, which took two months to notice.

— Dmitri, infrastructure
